problems.title: Length of a spatial vector
problems.question: Find the length of $(-3,3,-2)$.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
steps: The length is $\sqrt{9+9+4}=\sqrt{22}$.

problems.title: Angle with an axis and its positive direction
problems.question: Find the cosine between $m=(-3,\sqrt3,-2)$ and the $z$ axis.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
steps: The smaller angle with the undirected axis has cosine $|m_z|/|m|=2/4=1/2$, the listed choice.
If the positive $z$ direction is intended, the directional cosine instead is $m_z/|m|=-1/2$.
problems.answer: $1/2$ for the smaller axis-line angle; $-1/2$ with the positive axis direction.
problems.note: The source lists only +1/2. The distinction matters because the vector’s z component is negative.

problems.title: A square root gives one valid root
problems.question: Find the sum of real solutions of $\sqrt{x+5}+1=x$.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: $\sqrt{x+5}=x-1$ requires $x\ge1$.
steps: Square to obtain $x+5=(x-1)^2$, or $(x-4)(x+1)=0$.
Only $x=4$ meets the sign restriction and original equation. The sum is 4.

problems.title: Rotate a point through one hundred fifty degrees
problems.question: Rotate $(-\sqrt3,1)$ counterclockwise by $150^\circ$ about the origin.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: $X=x\cos\theta-y\sin\theta$, $Y=x\sin\theta+y\cos\theta$.
steps: Use $\cos150^\circ=-\sqrt3/2$, $\sin150^\circ=1/2$. Then $X=3/2-1/2=1$ and $Y=-\sqrt3/2-\sqrt3/2=-\sqrt3$.

problems.title: One white ball and one black ball
problems.question: A box contains 2 red,3 black,4 white balls. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability of one white and one black.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Favourable unordered pairs $=4\cdot3$; total pairs $=\binom92$.
steps: The probability is $12/36=1/3$.

problems.title: Dot product of two cross products
problems.question: $x=(1,1,1)\times(1,1,2)$, $y=(1,1,3)\times(2,1,1)$. Find $x\cdot y$.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Compute a cross product by the signed coordinate minors.

problems.title: A purported minimum is unbounded below
problems.question: Find the minimum of $x+y$ subject to $y\ge x$, $y\le-2x+3$, $y\ge x/2+1$.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: A family of feasible points with objective tending to $-\infty$ proves there is no finite minimum.
steps: For any $t\ge0$, set $x=-t$, $y=1-t/2$. The third inequality is equality, the first holds since $y-x=1+t/2>0$, and the second holds since $1-t/2\le2t+3$.
At these feasible points, $x+y=1-3t/2$, which decreases without limit as $t$ increases.
problems.answer: No finite minimum; the expression is unbounded below.
problems.note: None of the printed finite answer choices follows from the stated inequalities. No extra x≥0 condition or reversed inequality is assumed.

problems.title: Existence of a cosine equation solution
problems.question: For which $a$ does $\cos(1-2x)=2a-1$ have a real solution?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Cosine takes every value in $[-1,1]$.
steps: Require $-1\le2a-1\le1$, equivalent to $0\le a\le1$. Since $1-2x$ ranges over all real numbers, this condition is sufficient too.

problems.title: A phase parameter giving a cosine maximum
problems.question: Find the greatest negative $a$ such that $\cos(6x-\pi a/7)$ is maximal at $x=\pi$.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Cosine equals its maximum 1 exactly at integer multiples of $2\pi$.
steps: $6\pi-\pi a/7=2k\pi$ gives $a=42-14k$. These are multiples of 14.
The greatest strictly negative one is $-14$.

problems.title: Pay an amount using ones and fives
problems.question: How many ways can 29 units be paid using only 1-unit and 5-unit coins?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Nonnegative counts satisfy $u+5v=29$.
steps: The count of five-unit coins can be $v=0,1,2,3,4,5$. Each choice uniquely determines $u=29-5v$.

problems.title: A positive parameter for perpendicular vectors
problems.question: Find positive $x$ such that $(x,x,-1)$ and $(1,x-2,2)$ are perpendicular.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: The dot product must vanish.
steps: The positive root is $x=2$.

problems.title: Middle term of an even-power binomial
problems.question: Find the middle term of $(x^{-1/5}+x^{1/3})^{10}$.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: There are 11 terms, so the middle is $T_6=\binom{10}5u^5v^5$.

problems.title: Simplify a combinatorial equation
problems.question: Solve $\binom{n+4}{n+1}+\binom{n+3}n=13(n+2)(n+3)/6$ for natural $n$.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Use symmetry: the two coefficients are $\binom{n+4}3,\binom{n+3}3$.
steps: The sum factors as $(n+2)(n+3)[(n+4)+(n+1)]/6$.
Cancel the positive common factors to obtain $2n+5=13$, hence $n=4$.

problems.title: Four students assigned to four classes
problems.question: Four students independently choose uniformly among four classes. Find the probability they all enter different classes.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Total assignments $=4^4$; all-different assignments $=4!$.
steps: The probability is $24/256=3/32$.

problems.title: A random right-hand side of a sine-cosine equation
problems.question: Choose $a$ uniformly from $[-7,8]$. Find the probability that $3\sin x+4\cos x=a$ has a solution.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: The range of $A\sin x+B\cos x$ is $[-\sqrt{A^2+B^2},\sqrt{A^2+B^2}]$.
steps: The attainable values form $[-5,5]$, length 10. The sampling interval has length 15.
The probability is $10/15=2/3$.

problems.title: Largest edge from three box face areas
problems.question: A rectangular box has face areas 4,9,16. Find its largest edge.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
steps: $c^2=36$, so $c=6$. The remaining edges are $8/3$ and $3/2$, both smaller.

problems.title: The shortest path touching a straight bank
problems.question: Two tree tops are 3 m and 5 m above a straight bank, and their bases are 15 m apart. A bird touches point $K$ on the bank between them. Minimize the path from one top via $K$ to the other.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Reflect one endpoint across the bank; the shortest broken path becomes a straight segment.
steps: After reflecting the 3 m top below the bank, the vertical separation from the 5 m top is 8 m and horizontal separation 15 m.
The straight distance is $\sqrt{15^2+8^2}=17$. Its crossing point lies between the bases, so this bound is attainable.

problems.title: Three-digit numbers with a repeated digit
problems.question: How many three-digit natural numbers contain at least two equal digits?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Count the complement among 900 three-digit numbers.
steps: For all distinct digits, the hundreds digit has 9 choices, the tens digit 9 remaining choices including zero, and units digit 8.
The complement count is $9\cdot9\cdot8=648$. Thus repeated-digit numbers total $900-648=252$.

problems.title: Integer solutions of a radical inequality
problems.question: How many integers satisfy $\sqrt{2x+3}\ge x$?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Domain $x\ge-3/2$; for $x\ge0$ squaring preserves the inequality.
steps: All domain points with $x\le0$ satisfy it. For $x\ge0$, require $x^2-2x-3\le0$, giving $0\le x\le3$.
The full set is $[-3/2,3]$, containing integers $-1,0,1,2,3$.

problems.title: Area of a triangle in a horizontal plane
problems.question: $A=(1,1,1),B=(1,7,1),C=(8,0,1)$. Find $[ABC]$.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: All points have $z=1$, so use planar base-height area.
steps: $AB$ has length 6 along the $y$ direction. Point $C$ is distance $8-1=7$ from its line in that plane.
The area is $6\cdot7/2=21$.

problems.title: A square root bounded by a negative variable
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt{x+2}\le-x$.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: The domain and right-side sign require $-2\le x\le0$.
steps: Square on that interval: $x+2\le x^2$, or $(x-2)(x+1)\ge0$.
Intersect $x\le-1$ or $x\ge2$ with the domain to obtain $[-2,-1]$.

problems.title: Image of a line under a homothety
problems.question: A homothety centred at the origin has scale 3. Find the image of $y=-x+2$.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Image coordinates satisfy $X=3x,Y=3y$.
steps: Substitute $x=X/3,y=Y/3$: $Y/3=-X/3+2$. Hence $Y=-X+6$.

problems.title: Perpendicular lines in a cube
problems.question: In cube $ABCDA_1B_1C_1D_1$, $M$ is midpoint of $B_1C_1$ and $K$ midpoint of $CC_1$. Find the angle between $AM,B_1K$.
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: Perpendicular vectors have zero dot product.
steps: Directions $AM=(1,1/2,1)$ and $B_1K=(0,1,-1/2)$ have dot product $1/2-1/2=0$.

problems.title: Infer a dismissal rate from a conditional probability
problems.question: 80% of employees are diligent and 20% lazy. 10% of the diligent are dismissed. Among dismissed employees, 32% are diligent. What percentage of lazy employees are dismissed?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: $P(D\cap F)=P(D)P(F\mid D)$; $P(D\mid F)=P(D\cap F)/P(F)$.
steps: The diligent-dismissed fraction of the workforce is $0.8\cdot0.1=0.08$. Thus total dismissed fraction is $0.08/0.32=0.25$.
The lazy-dismissed fraction is $0.25-0.08=0.17$. Relative to the lazy 0.2, its rate is $0.17/0.2=0.85$.

problems.title: A vector angle obtuse for every real input
problems.question: Which listed $a$ makes the angle between $(x,1,a)$ and $(-x,2x,3)$ obtuse for every real $x$?
problems.idea: Translate the conditions into equations and retain the relevant signs and domains.
formulas: An obtuse angle requires a negative dot product.
steps: The dot product is $-x^2+2x+3a=-(x-1)^2+1+3a$. Its maximum over $x$ is $1+3a$.
This must be strictly negative, so $a<-1/3$. Of the listed values, only $a=-0.5$ qualifies.
